answer: A caught sybil stains its neighbours. Rather than delete a thousand keys, the registry marks each signed edge and lets the stain spread, thinning with distance like a comet's tail. A dense farm saturates its component, so all members wake tainted. An edge clears only when its owner works with an outside party, and clearing decays: an idle key fogs over in a few epochs. Honest agents lose little, since a violet smudge rubs off with the next job, but a cluster must buy an outsider's signature for every edge, each epoch. Hiding becomes permanent upkeep; a lone cedar outside stays clean.
